raw_prompt: Implement an atomic financial ledger transaction with debit/credit balance invariance and idempotency check.

cumulative_requirements.title: Atomic Financial Ledger Transaction
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must execute financial ledger entries as an atomic transaction ensuring all-or-nothing persistence across multi-legged entries.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Directly requested in prompt: 'Implement an atomic financial ledger transaction'.

cumulative_requirements.title: Debit and Credit Balance Invariance
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must enforce double-entry bookkeeping balance invariance where the sum of debits must equal the sum of credits for every committed transaction.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Directly requested in prompt: 'debit/credit balance invariance'.

cumulative_requirements.title: Idempotency Check
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must perform an idempotency check prior to transaction processing to prevent duplicate execution of identical transaction requests.

cumulative_requirements.title: Idempotency Key Persistence and Uniqueness Constraint
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must store idempotency keys alongside request hashes with a strict database unique constraint.
cumulative_requirements.justification:
Why 1 (Context/Risk): Without persistent uniqueness checks, concurrent duplicate requests can bypass application-layer memory checks.
Why 2 (Technical Mechanism): A unique database constraint on the idempotency key column guarantees database-level race condition prevention.
Why 3 (Mandatory Invariant): The system must never process duplicate transaction requests under concurrent load.

cumulative_requirements.title: ACID Database Isolation for Balance Updates
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must execute balance reads and writes using serializable or repeatable read isolation levels to prevent lost updates.
cumulative_requirements.justification:
Why 1 (Context/Risk): Concurrent transactions against the same account balances can introduce race conditions leading to negative balances or corrupt invariants.
Why 2 (Technical Mechanism): Utilizing row-level locking or strict database transaction isolation prevents interleaved updates.
Why 3 (Mandatory Invariant): Account balance invariants and double-entry balancing must hold true under high-concurrency conditions.

cumulative_requirements.title: Idempotency Key Expiration Window
cumulative_requirements.description: The retention period or time-to-live (TTL) for idempotency keys is unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify how long idempotency keys must be retained before expiration.

cumulative_requirements.title: Ledger Storage Technology and Schema
cumulative_requirements.description: The specific database engine, storage provider, and schema design for the ledger are unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: No specific database technology or schema layout was provided in the prompt.

cumulative_requirements.title: Account Balance Floor Enforcement and Overdraft Prevention
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must validate that source accounts do not violate minimum balance or overdraft limits prior to committing a debit entry, unless an explicit credit line or overdraft facility is authorized.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: The prompt mandates an atomic financial ledger transaction with debit/credit balance invariance. Step 2: In double-entry bookkeeping, balancing journal entries alone does not prevent individual accounts from dropping below legally or operationally mandated minimums (e.g., negative balances without credit facilities). Step 3: Therefore, a balance floor check must be integrated into the atomic transaction validation phase to maintain account solvency and domain invariants.

cumulative_requirements.title: Deadlock Prevention and Timeout Guard for Concurrent Ledger Locking
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must acquire account locks in a deterministic, globally sorted order (e.g., sorting account IDs lexicographically) and enforce strict statement timeouts to prevent circular wait deadlocks during concurrent multi-account transfers.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: Concurrent transactions modifying overlapping sets of source and destination accounts under high isolation levels are prone to deadlocks. Step 2: Unmanaged deadlocks lead to transaction aborts, resource exhaustion, and degraded availability. Step 3: Therefore, deterministic lock ordering and timeout guards must be implemented to ensure safe and predictable concurrent execution.

cumulative_requirements.title: Immutable Ledger Audit Trail and Append-Only Enforcement
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must prohibit UPDATE and DELETE operations on committed ledger transaction rows, ensuring that any corrections or reversals are executed strictly via compensating entries.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Step 1: Financial ledgers require strict regulatory compliance and tamper-evident audit trails. Step 2: Allowing direct modifications or deletions of committed ledger entries destroys historical provenance and breaks double-entry auditability. Step 3: Therefore, the database schema and application logic must enforce append-only immutability for all historical ledger records.

cumulative_requirements.title: Network Transport and API Protocol Unstated
cumulative_requirements.description: The exact transport protocol (e.g., HTTPS/TLS 1.3, gRPC over HTTP/2) and message framing format for submitting ledger transactions are unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: No network layer or serialization protocol has been specified in prior passes.

cumulative_requirements.title: Authentication and Authorization Provider Unstated
cumulative_requirements.description: The identity provider, token format (e.g., OAuth2 JWT, mTLS), and role-based access control (RBAC) mechanisms for authorizing ledger entries are unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Authentication boundary and security principals have not been defined in prior passes.

cumulative_requirements.title: Crash Recovery and In-Flight Transaction Resolution
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must utilize write-ahead logging (WAL) and two-phase commit or transactional outbox recovery protocols to roll back uncommitted in-flight transactions or safely reconcile doubtful states upon unexpected power loss or process crash.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Operational lifecycle requirement for financial systems to guarantee atomicity and durability (ACID 'D') across sudden infrastructure failures.

cumulative_requirements.title: Statutory Financial Record Retention Compliance
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must retain all immutable ledger audit trail records and transaction histories for a minimum statutory period (e.g., 5 to 7 years depending on jurisdiction) in compliance with financial regulations like Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) or the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA).
cumulative_requirements.justification: Statutory regulatory invariant mandatory for any financial ledger system operating within standard regulatory jurisdictions.
